note: Found on 2026-10-02. A Schlumberger sounding that reads 1444.3 ohm-m at every spacing, a uniform half-space. The layer search starts at two layers (VESConfig.min_layers = 2), both engines fit two layers of 1444.3 ohm-m to a misfit of 1e-14 percent, and the boundary between them is wherever each optimiser left it: 0.5 m in Python, 0.7 m in the browser. Any depth fits equally well, so neither is wrong against the other and loosening the tolerance would hide nothing worth hiding.
open: What should a layered inversion report for a sounding with no layering: a one-layer model (which interpretation, design and the reports would all have to accept), two layers with the boundary marked unresolved, or a refusal? Until that is decided the two engines report different, equally meaningless, boundary depths for a uniform half-space.
